context.projectOverview: Make PgeEngine able to execute a realistic plan at all — today every channel caps at 4,096 bytes while this repository's own PlanSpec is 29,247, so plan_materialize's writes are silently dropped and the run proceeds with state.spec null. Then give the engine a way to report that a run did not do what it claims: a fail-closed refusal of the git-effect commit node currently returns success: true because PipelineResult has no error channel.

contract.title: Size the caps to the corpus, regenerate the artifact, pin both directions
contract.description: The decided remedy: raise every implicated channel's maxInlineBytes to a value derived from the committed corpus, keep StateBloatError as a guard against genuinely runaway writes, regenerate the artifact and the state audit, take a MINOR graphVersion bump with a changelog entry, and pin each cap two-directionally against the corpus so that neither shrinking nor inflating one can happen silently.

successCriteria.description: src/pge/topology/coding.graph.ts declares, for every channel the measurement implicates, a maxInlineBytes at least the corpus maximum for that channel, and .bober/topology/coding.json is regenerated from it via `pge dump`.
graphVersion takes a MINOR bump and docs/pge-graph.md gains a changelog entry keyed by it, stating which caps moved and the measured basis for each.

`pge dump --check`, `pge validate --mode full`, `pge docs --check`, `pge diff --require-version-bump` and `pge audit-state` followed by `git diff --exit-code` all pass against the regenerated artifact and the regenerated state audit.

A test pins each cap two-directionally against the committed corpus: lowering a cap below its corpus maximum FAILS, and raising a cap with no corpus payload justifying it FAILS. Both directions proven by mutation.
A negative control proves StateBloatError still bites: a value above the NEW cap is still rejected and the write is still dropped, so the check was re-sized rather than removed.
The golden dataset still passes unchanged -- a MINOR bump does not invalidate cases, and no golden file is edited in this sprint.
Full suite, typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build are green.

nonGoals: Removing or weakening the StateBloatError check.
Adding the specDraft channel, which is sprint 7.

Editing a golden case for any reason OTHER than refreshing the graph.graphVersion stamp after this sprint's MINOR bump. The recapture is authorised ONLY if the diff is exactly that one field per case and nothing else; any other field moving is a stop condition.
stopConditions: The golden dataset fails after the cap change -- stop and report; a MINOR cap bump should not move any recorded artifact, and if it does, that is a defect worth understanding before proceeding.
`pge diff` reports the change as MAJOR rather than MINOR -- stop and reconsider the classification rather than forcing the bump.
contract.definitionOfDone: All required criteria met, the full suite plus typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build are green, and every documentation claim added is backed by a test that fails when the claim stops being true.
assumptions: HEADROOM SCHEME (resolves the tension in sc-3-4, designed by the curator, adopt unless you find it wrong): pin each cap as EQUALITY to a pure derived function of the corpus, capForCorpusMax(corpusMax) = the next power of two at or above 2x corpusMax, floored at DEFAULT_MAX_INLINE_BYTES. This satisfies BOTH directions of sc-3-4 because the cap is a FUNCTION of the corpus rather than a literal: lowering below the corpus max and inflating without justification both break the equality. It also absorbs the messages/evaluations resampling drift within a power-of-two bucket. Under it only two caps move: spec 48,097 -> 131,072 and sprintContracts 135,106 -> 524,288; the other eight channels stay at exactly 4,096.

SIZE FROM 48,097, NOT 29,214. Two spec-channel maxima appear in the docs and both are correct: 29,214 is THIS repository's own PGE spec (sprint 1) and 48,097 is the largest of all 52 parsing specs (sprint 2). The cap must accommodate the largest real spec.

pge diff has NO MAJOR/MINOR classifier — verified. src/pge/topology/diff.ts:231-240 exposes only isVersionBumped, a forward-move check. The sprint's MAJOR stop condition is therefore unsatisfiable, and the golden dataset's MAJOR-only integrity check (case-schema.ts:371-377) survives a bump to 1.3.0.

FOUR BLOCKERS OUTSIDE THE ORIGINAL estimatedFiles, verified by the orchestrator — a cap or version change reddens all of them: (a) src/pge/engine/real-workload.test.ts hardcodes 4096 in about seven assertions and byte-compares the committed measurement; (b) src/pge/topology/coding.graph.test.ts:117 pins graphVersion to "1.2.0"; (c) src/pge/topology/docs.test.ts:971 pins changelogVersions to exactly ["1.2.0","1.1.0","1.0.0"] AND its negative control at :975 uses the LITERAL "1.3.0" as its "version the changelog does not mention" fixture — so adding a 1.3.0 changelog entry breaks the very test that guards the pairing, and that fixture must be re-keyed to an unused version; (d) the render fixtures src/pge/topology/__fixtures__/coding.mermaid and coding.dot are byte-pinned on the version header and need regenerating.

The measurement artifact .bober/topology/measurements/real-workload.json is owned by sprint 4, which regenerates it to show the rejections gone. This sprint may need to touch it; if so, keep the change minimal and say so.
contract.generatorNotes: Edit the AUTHORED literal at src/pge/topology/coding.graph.ts:113-190, then regenerate the committed JSON with the pge CLI -- never hand-edit .bober/topology/coding.json, which `pge dump --check` will catch anyway. Pick caps from the corpus with deliberate headroom and say in the code comment what the headroom is for; a cap that exactly equals today's maximum will fail the day a spec grows one field. Keep StateBloatError: the point is to size the guard, not to delete it. Remember the state audit is a committed artifact gated by `pge audit-state` plus `git diff --exit-code` (src/pge/audit-git-gate.test.ts), so regenerate it in the same commit.
contract.evaluatorNotes: Verify the two-directional pin genuinely bites in BOTH directions by mutating it yourself -- lower a cap below corpus max and confirm failure, then raise one arbitrarily and confirm failure. A pin that only catches shrinkage is half a pin. Verify the negative control for StateBloatError by constructing a value above the new cap and confirming the write is dropped and a StateBloatError lands in `rejected`. Confirm .bober/topology/coding.json was regenerated rather than hand-edited by running `pge dump --check` yourself. Confirm the changelog entry states a MEASURED basis per cap, not a round number with no provenance.

principles:
# Project Principles

> These principles guide all planning, generation, and evaluation in the Bober pipeline.
> Updated: 2026-04-16

## Mission

Agent-bober is a multi-agent harness that builds applications autonomously using any LLM. It orchestrates a pipeline of specialized agents (Researcher, Planner, Curator, Generator, Evaluator) and supports Claude, GPT, Gemini, and Ollama. It ships as an npm CLI + MCP server for Claude Code, Cursor, and Windsurf.

## Users

- **Primary:** Developers using Claude Code, Cursor, or Windsurf who want autonomous feature generation with quality gates
- **Secondary:** Teams integrating agent-bober programmatically via the TypeScript API or MCP server
- Technical level: intermediate to advanced — users understand LLMs, CI/CD, and modern JS tooling

## Quality Standards

- **Type safety:** TypeScript strict mode with all strict flags (`noUnusedLocals`, `noUnusedParameters`, `noImplicitReturns`, `noFallthroughCasesInSwitch`, `isolatedModules`). Zero type errors is a hard gate.
- **Lint compliance:** ESLint flat config with `consistent-type-imports` enforced, `no-explicit-any` warned, unused vars errored (with `_` prefix escape). Zero lint errors is a hard gate.
- **Test coverage:** Vitest for unit tests. Tests are collocated with source (`*.test.ts` next to `*.ts`). Tests run against the real project when practical (e.g., scanner tests scan agent-bober itself).
- **Build integrity:** `tsc` must produce clean output. Build is a required evaluator strategy.

## Technical Principles

### Follow

- **ESM everywhere.** `"type": "module"` in package.json. All imports use `.js` extensions for NodeNext resolution. No CommonJS.
- **Provider-agnostic interfaces.** All LLM interaction goes through `providers/types.ts` — provider-specific SDKs are wrapped by adapters (`anthropic.ts`, `openai.ts`, `google.ts`). Never leak SDK types outside adapter files.
- **Zod for config validation.** All configuration schemas are Zod schemas in `config/schema.ts`. Runtime config loading uses `z.parse()`. No hand-rolled validation.
- **Contract-based architecture.** PlanSpecs, SprintContracts, and EvalResults are the communication protocol between agents. They live in `contracts/` and are JSON files on disk in `.bober/`.
- **Filesystem state.** All mutable state (specs, contracts, handoffs, eval results, history) is stored as JSON files in `.bober/`. No database, no in-memory global state.
- **Section comments.** Use unicode box-drawing section headers: `// -- Section Name ------` to organize long files.
- **Small utility modules.** Utils in `utils/` are focused single-purpose files (`fs.ts`, `git.ts`, `logger.ts`). Keep them small.
- **Conventional commits.** Format: `type: description` where type is `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `release`, `refactor`, `test`, `chore`. Sprint-generated commits use `bober(sprint-N): description`.
- **Use `type` imports.** ESLint enforces `consistent-type-imports` -- import types with `import type { ... }` syntax.
- **Prefix unused params with `_`.** The `_` prefix is the only escape hatch for unused variables/parameters.

### Avoid

- **No `any` without justification.** `no-explicit-any` is a warning; aim for zero. Use `unknown` + type narrowing instead.
- **No SDK lock-in.** Never import `@anthropic-ai/sdk` or `openai` outside of their respective adapter files in `providers/`.
- **No synchronous filesystem ops.** All fs operations use `node:fs/promises`. No `fs.readFileSync` etc.
- **No barrel re-exports for deep internals.** `src/index.ts` exports the public API only. Internal modules import directly.
- **No test mocks for filesystem.** Tests that need filesystem state create temp directories and clean up. The scanner tests run against the real codebase.

## Design Principles

N/A -- no user interface. Agent-bober is a CLI tool and programmatic library. The MCP server exposes tools, not UI.

blockers.test: src/pge/golden/capture.test.ts — 5 replay cases fail 'is exactly what a fresh capture produces'
blockers.rootCause: A fresh capture embeds the CURRENT graphVersion into the case; the comparison is byte-exact. The diff is exactly one field per case: graph.graphVersion 1.2.0 -> 1.3.0.
blockers.orchestratorDecision: RECAPTURE THE FIVE CASES. The nonGoal forbidding it has been narrowed for exactly this. Rationale: the case's graph.graphVersion is a FACT about what the case was recorded against, so leaving five files claiming 1.2.0 while they validate against 1.3.0 puts a stale fact in the dataset — worse than a one-field diff. Do NOT instead loosen capture.test.ts's byte comparison: byte-exactness is the stronger gate and NFR0 forbids weakening one to go green. VERIFY the diff is exactly graph.graphVersion on each of the five and nothing else; if any other field moves, STOP and report — that would mean the cap change altered a recorded artifact, which is a real finding. Also record in docs/pge-graph.md that a MINOR bump requires a replay recapture, noting the tension with case-schema.ts:348-357's MAJOR-only rule, which was written to avoid exactly this cost.

blockers.test: src/pge/golden/workload.test.ts — 'every file-group sprintContracts entry equals the array its own paths parse to'
blockers.rootCause: The corpus entry sprintContracts-spec-20260812-pge-real-workload-errors is a snapshot of THIS spec's own contract files. The orchestrator writes status/completedAt/iterationHistory into those contracts as each sprint completes, so the snapshot goes stale DURING the very run that built it. This is not pre-existing noise — it is a self-reference defect in the corpus.
blockers.orchestratorDecision: FIX IT PROPERLY: exclude the in-flight spec's own contracts from the corpus (or otherwise make the corpus not snapshot artifacts the running pipeline mutates), then regenerate the affected entries. A corpus that invalidates itself as the pipeline runs cannot serve as the permanent workload tier sprint 3's cap pin depends on. State in the code WHY the exclusion exists so nobody re-adds it.

recordOnlyDoNotChase.finding: With the caps raised, the run gets past plan_materialize and into the 14-contract fan-out, then throws SuperstepLimitExceededError at DEFAULT_MAX_SUPERSTEPS=200 (interpreter.ts:386,1060) before reaching any terminal node. The byte cap was masking this — the two defects only ever looked like one symptom ('never reaches a terminal'). This is sprint 4's territory. Keep it recorded in the measurement and docs; do NOT attempt to fix it here.
